question: An engineer must configure the order in which the server attempts to boot from available boot device types using Cisco Integrated Management Controller (Cisco IMC). The engineer must change the boot order configuration during the setup and apply the new requirements multiple times. The requirement is to change the Cisco IMC actual boot order so it is different from the configured boot order. Which setting accomplishes this goal?
options: Enable the system to boot with the configured boot order.
Set the boot configuration directly through BIOS.
Apply UEFI Secure Boot for a nonsupported operating system.
Configure the legacy and precision boot order to be mutually exclusive.
theory: Cisco IMC lets an administrator temporarily override the configured (persistent) boot order for the very next boot by setting the boot device order directly through the BIOS setup utility at POST time, without permanently altering the saved boot policy. This is exactly the mechanism needed when the actual boot sequence for one specific boot must differ from what's normally configured, and it can be repeated on demand each time the server boots, unlike toggling UEFI secure boot or boot-mode exclusivity settings, which address different concerns. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — Cisco IMC Boot Order Management)
